strategies.overview: Tentacruel is a role-compression extraordinaire, with access to a myriad of utility moves like Knock Off, Rapid Spin, and Haze all in a neatly packed bulky Water-type that is immune to Toxic and can pivot with Flip Turn. Tentacruel's typing lets it take on many threats like Paldean Tauros-F, Inteleon, and Sylveon. Tentacruel also has a niche in thwarting HP-draining attacks like Uxie's Draining Kiss and Brambleghast's Strength Sap thanks to Liquid Ooze. Although Tentacruel boasts a lot of utility options, it's quite passive and can often get overwhelmed attempting to make use of every support move in a battle. Because of this, Tentacruel is best used as a bulky pivot to allow powerful wallbreakers like Porygon-Z and Flamigo to hit the field safely. Despite its great typing and Special Defense, Tentacruel's lack of recovery and poor physical bulk often leave it getting overwhelmed quite easily.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Tentacruel can use Acid Spray as a way to combat bulky setup sweepers such as Scrafty and Vaporeon while still retaining a sliver of an offensive presence. Using its defensive typing and Speed boost from Rapid Spin, Tentacruel can use Swords Dance with powerful physical moves like Gunk Shot and Knock Off, even ignoring Intimidate via Clear Body. Tentacruel's other ability, Rain Dish, can let it take advantage of either the opponent's rain or find itself on a rain team.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Although Tentacruel is a Water-type, with only a weak Flip Turn in its arsenal, many Ground-types like Flygon and Swampert can safely pivot into Tentacruel and threaten to OHKO it with Earthquake.

Item Removal: Without Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, Tentacruel has no method of recovery and will fail as a long-term pivot and entry hazard remover, making it quite reliant on its item. Even Pokemon it's meant to check like Infernape and opposing Tentacruel can dissuade Tentacruel from coming in for fear of Knock Off.

movesets.name: Defensive Pivot
movesets.description:
Set Details

Tentacruel may want to delay using Rapid Spin if it has been hit with Leech Seed, as this will deal constant damage to the foe. Knock Off is Tentacruel's primary way of not being entirely passive, removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from Pokemon that can switch into it like Swampert and Klefki. Haze disrupts bulky setup sweepers. Toxic achieves a similar goal, but Tentacruel must be wary of Tera Poison and Steel commonly seen on bulky setup sweepers like Calm Mind Sylveon and Scrafty. Toxic is also useless against the many bulky Steel-types like Bronzong and Registeel using IronPress, Poison-types like Overqwil and Toxicroak, and Substitute users like Uxie and Paldean Tauros-W. Toxic Spikes make pivots into Tentacruel riskier, especially if it has previously removed Heavy-Duty Boots; however, the metagame is teeming with airborne foes, grounded Poison-types, and Heavy-Duty Boots users. Lastly, Sludge Bomb gives Tentacruel a means of dealing out any meaningful damage, letting it 2HKO Grass-types like Tsareena and Breloom that can otherwise take advantage of Tentacruel and threaten frailer offensive threats like Paldean Tauros-W and Porygon-Z. The given EV spread lets it outpace base 85 Speed Pokemon like Heracross and Overqwil, although this can be lowered to only outspeed foes with base 80 Speed and below like Chandelure, Basculegion-M, and Milotic or raised to outspeed even the likes of Porygon-Z and Hisuian Typhlosion.

Tentacruel's ability to pivot in and out of play easily facilitates frail wallbreakers like Porygon-Z, Flamigo, and Breloom, which can take advantage of bulky Water-types that often switch in on Tentacruel like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Gastrodon. Bronzong and Orthworm pair well with Tentacruel, serving as Ground-immune and Psychic-resistant Pokemon that can set up entry hazards for Tentacruel. They also appreciate Tentacruel's Fire resistance, allowing it to check threats like Chandelure and Infernape. Offensive pivots such as Flygon and Kilowattrel are two Ground-immune Pokemon that also offer an Electric immunity for Tentacruel as well. Defensive pivots like Gligar and Incineroar form nice VoltTurn cores with Tentacruel, and their respective immense physical bulk and Intimidate compensate for Tentacruel's poor Defense. Wish users like Sylveon and Florges can keep Tentacruel healthy as it sponges Poison-type attacks for them and bothers Amoonguss.

strategies.overview:
Poison

Tentacruel is a surprising option on Poison teams, as Toxapex's incredible bulk and longevity completely outclass it as a defensive wall in a majority of situations. However, Tentacruel has enough unique tools such that it could be worth considering over Toxapex should a more proactive Water-type threat be needed.
strategies.comments:
Other Options

Water

Knock Off synergizes well with Tentacruel's entry hazard-stacking, as it removes Heavy-Duty Boots from users such as Dragapult and Brambleghast. However, some of Tentacruel's teammates like Hisuian Samurott commonly run Knock Off as well. Protect allows Tentacruel to scout moves from Choice-locked Pokemon like Greninja, Meowscarada, and Gholdengo, but this comes at the cost of sacrificing some of Tentacruel's valuable role compression. Haze allows Tentacruel to better deal with Primarina and Sinistcha, but the limited amount of specific foes Haze targets is small enough that it isn't worth running over its main moves.

Poison

Ice Beam can be used over Knock Off and Protect to give Tentacruel more offensive pressure, allowing it to check threats like Adamant Dragonite after chip damage and Gliscor. Toxic can be used with Tentacruel's Speed to spread poison before going down.

movesets.name: Real Squid [Rapid Spin] (Poison)
movesets.description:
Tentacruel finds a niche on Poison teams thanks to a flurry of unique traits over its competition in Toxapex such as a vastly superior Speed stat and tools such as Rapid Spin, which makes Tentacruel the only form of entry hazard removal on Poison teams not weak to Steel-type attacks, allowing it to comfortably spin against foes such as Corviknight and Empoleon. Flip Turn allows Tentacruel to easily pivot out on foes such as Hisuian Samurott, Terapagos, and Gliscor. Knock Off is used in the final slot as a solid progress-making option, removing items from foes such as Skarmory and Gholdengo. However, Protect can be used to gain Black Sludge recovery and scout moves from foes. The defensive EVs for each spread provide different defensive benefits; the physically defensive spread with a Timid nature allows Tentacruel to survive an Earthquake from Gliscor and Dragonite, while the specially defensive spread with a Calm nature allows it to beat offensive Heatran and Iron Moth with Surf along with being able to reliably use Knock Off against Flutter Mane. The Speed EVs for both spreads allow Tentacruel to outspeed fully invested Pokemon with base 85 Speed such as Ceruledge, Terapagos, and Kleavor, allowing Tentacruel to reliably pivot out against them or threaten them with Surf and Knock Off.

Amoonguss serves as a solid defensive complement to Tentacruel, being able to handle Ground- and Electric-types such as Great Tusk, Sandy Shocks, and Rotom-W along with putting foes to sleep with Spore, allowing Tentacruel to come in safely and use Rapid Spin. Pecharunt provides solid defensive support by taking on powerful physical attackers like Azumarill, Galarian Zapdos, and Hisuain Arcanine. Overqwil enjoys Tentacruel's entry hazard removal not taking away Overqwil's hazards, and it supports Tentacruel by taking on threats such as Iron Boulder and Gallade. Alolan Muk handles special attackers such as Mew, Flutter Mane, and Terapagos. Galarian Slowking can handle high-power special threats such as Zapdos, Latios, and Choice Specs Iron Moth. Iron Moth appreciates Tentacruel removing entry hazards and pivoting it in with Flip Turn; in response, it can handle threats such as Alolan Ninetales, Gholdengo, and Articuno. Galarian Weezing appreciates Tentacruel's Rapid Spin allowing it to drop Defog, and in return, it provides a proper Ground immunity with Levitate and can take on threats such as Garchomp, Dragonite, and Iron Hands with Will-O-Wisp and Strange Steam. Okidogi and Sneasler can threaten Steel- and Dark-types like Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, Hisuian Samurott, and Hydreigon; Sneasler can pivot Tentacruel in safely via U-turn along with handling targets like Hoopa-U and Ogerpon-H, while Okidogi can use Bulk Up and beat threats such as Archaludon and Cloyster.

movesets.name: Rapid Spin (Water)
movesets.description:
Tentacruel is one of Water's best forms of role compression, removing entry hazards thanks to its access to Rapid Spin, absorbing Toxic Spikes placed by Toxapex and indirectly by Glimmora with its Poison typing, and slow pivoting with Flip Turn. Aside from this, its great ability in Liquid Ooze allows it to punish the Ogerpon formes and Sinistcha, which target it with Horn Leech and Matcha Gotcha. Furthermore, its part-Poison typing gives Water teams an option against Grass- and Fairy-types such as Breloom and Azumarill. Toxic Spikes aids its more offensive-based teammates by afflicting status on incoming foes, and due to Tentacruel's great defensive typing, it finds many opportunities to set one layer of Toxic Spikes. Flip Turn allows it to serve as a great pivot, as with its rather low Speed, it is able to almost always get a teammate in safely. A Calm nature along with 240 Special Defense EVs allows it to survive 2 Earth Powers from Choice Scarf Enamorus and 2 Fickle Beams from Nasty Plot-boosted Hydrapple. Alternatively, a Bold nature along with 240 Defense EVs allows it to survive a Swords Dance-boosted Horn Leech from the Ogerpon formes and KO back, as well as 2 Flower Tricks from Meowscarada. 16 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed Adamant Breloom, effectively checking it.

Hisuian Samurott forms an entry hazard-stacking core with Tentacruel, placing Spikes with Ceaseless Edge while bypassing Taunt and threatening Dark- and Psychic-types that threaten Tentacruel such as Bisharp and Latios. In return, Tentacruel handles Fairy-types for Hisuian Samurott. Poison-types such as Sneasler, Pecharunt, and Toxapex can come in to absorb Tentacruel's Toxic Spikes. Hence, Greninja makes for a great teammate, checking those Poison-types while also threatening bulky Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Clodsire. When Tentacruel is running a physically defensive EV spread, it forms a great defensive pairing with specially bulky Pokemon such as Swampert and Primarina. Swampert provides an Electric immunity, Stealth Rock support, and pivoting via Flip Turn, while Primarina takes on Dragon-types such as Latios, Latias, and Roaring Moon. Alomomola forms a defensive core with Tentacruel, as well as providing Tentacruel recovery via Wish. Tentacruel's ability to spread status and slow pivot is appreciated by late-game sweepers such as Ogerpon-W, Keldeo, and Urshifu-R. Ogerpon-W takes on Landorus, while Keldeo and Urshifu-R break through Steel-types like Archaludon, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon. Rotom-W can switch in against Ground-types thanks to Levitate, and it also threatens common hazard removers like Corviknight and Great Tusk with its STAB moves.

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 5 onwards

Price Range: 8-9 points

Overview: Tentacruel is a solid form of entry hazard control that can both set and remove entry hazards to help support its teammates. It's also blessed by having a great utility movepool on top of this, which turns it into a very solid support Pokemon. However, it's held back by having incredibly common and exploitable weaknesses and no reliable recovery, as well as tending to overlap too heavily with better, more expensive Pokemon. For these reasons, Tentacruel is never going to be your first choice for its roles, but it can serve as a very valuable backup.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Utility Support: Tentacruel utilizes its vast movepool, from Toxic Spikes to Knock Off to Flip Turn with many more in between, acting as a great enabler for its teammates. It can be especially disruptive against teams with poor entry hazard removal, as it's able to both remove hazards from its own side and set them on the other.

Specially Defensive Wall: Typically paired with an Assault Vest to enhance its already-great Special Defense, Tentacruel is able to check nearly all special attackers and force them to take a strong hit, thanks to Mirror Coat.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Surf, Hydro Pump, Sludge Bomb, Sludge Wave, Gunk Shot

Setup Moves: Acid Armor, Acid Spray

Utility Moves: Toxic, Toxic Spikes, Rapid Spin, Knock Off, Flip Turn, Mirror Coat, Haze, Chilling Water, Icy Wind, Whirlpool, Reflect Type

Coverage: Dazzling Gleam, Giga Drain, Hex, Ice Beam, Tera Blast, Weather Ball

Niche Moves

Swords Dance: Despite its relatively low Attack, Swords Dance Tentacruel is able to punch holes through specially defensive teams due to the combination of its surprise factor and good STAB moves such as Gunk Shot and Liquidation, especially when powered up by a Life Orb.

Common Items

Heavy-Duty Boots: The standard item of choice, it grants Tentacruel the longevity to safely come in and fulfill its role as support for its teammates.

Black Sludge / Leftovers: Against teams with poor entry hazard setters, Tentacruel benefits more from the passive recovery granted by Black Sludge and Leftovers, especially if they are paired with Protect. Black Sludge is nearly always optimal, but Leftovers is better when Tentacruel is a Tera Captain.

Assault Vest: Assault Vest allows Tentacruel to act as a sponge for most special hits, which works well in conjunction with Mirror Coat.

Niche Items

Rocky Helmet: Due to resisting Bug, Tentacruel can be used to punish most U-turn spammers with Rocky Helmet.

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is a sidegrade to Black Sludge / Leftovers in games where Tentacruel is expected to only have to take a handful of hits, usually in quick succession.

Tera

Tentacruel should rarely, if ever, be considered as a Tera Captain. Its teammates nearly always benefit from Tera more than it does. In the event that you still make it a Tera Captain, it can utilize types such as Grass, Steel, and Ground defensively, as well as benefitting from Tera Blast Electric and Dark offensively.

Draft Strategy

Tentacruel is never something one plans for going into the draft, but it can find itself fitting well alongside the following kinds of Pokemon.

Entry Hazard-weak Wallbreakers: Tentacruel is able to be a reliable entry hazard remover and can pivot, making it a great partner alongside the likes of Chi-Yu, Enamorus, and Weavile.

Physical Bulk: Tentacruel's key weakness is its poor Defense, offsetting its specially defensive prowess. It can form a strong backbone alongside traditionally physically defensive tanks and walls such as Landorus-T, Skarmory, and Iron Hands.

Fighting-type Answers: While Tentacruel resists Fighting, it often finds itself vulnerable to Fighting-types as a whole due to its poor physical bulk. It works well in conjunction with Pokemon such as Scream Tail, Uxie, and Zapdos for this reason.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Tentacruel finds itself in a tough spot when trying to remove entry hazards, as it becomes a free switch in for Electric-types such as Zapdos, Raging Bolt, and Iron Hands. It's unable to punish them effectively and is thus forced out, putting its user on the back foot.

Physical Attackers: Tentacruel's poor Defense means that it's unable to deal with strong physical attackers such as Baxcalibur and Ogerpon and is even 2HKOed by resisted hits such as Palafin's Wave Crash.

Taunt: Due to Tentacruel's poor offensive stats and reliance on Toxic and Toxic Spikes to help make progress against bulkier teams, it is incredibly susceptible to Taunt.

Poison- and Steel-types: Since they both resist or are immune to Sludge Bomb and Toxic, most Poison- and Steel-types can switch in safely on Tentacruel. They tend to not fear its Water-type attacks and usually take very little damage from coverage moves, causing Tentacruel to become deadweight against them.
